meaning: of Bicker-dike, i.e. 'the dike of Bicker,' Bicker representing an early personal name
author_comment: I cannot find the spot. Evidently it means 'the dike of Bicker,' Bicker representing an early personal name, as is proved by such place-names as Bickerton (in cos. Chester, York, Northumberland), Bickerston (co. Norfolk), Bickering (co. Lincoln), and Bickerstaffe (co. Lancashire). Probably Lincolnshire is the home of this surname.
source: History of Norfolk (Blomefield and Parkin), vol. iv, p. 206
record_text: 1701. Nicholas Bickerdik, Norwich: FF. iv. 206.
